# Physical activity and cancer risk

## Abstract

This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled prospective cohort studies of leisure-time physical activity and cancer incidence in adults. Higher levels of physical activity were associated with a lower risk of colon cancer, breast cancer and endometrial cancer. The associations were consistent across studies and remained after adjustment for body mass index.

## Results

Compared with the least active participants, the most active participants had a lower risk of colon cancer. The reduction in risk was also observed for breast cancer in postmenopausal women and for endometrial cancer. A dose-response relationship was observed: more activity was associated with a lower risk, and even modest amounts of activity were associated with some benefit.

## Conclusions

Regular physical activity is associated with a lower risk of several common cancers. Public health strategies that help people become more active may contribute to cancer prevention.
